subject: Modeling and fitting a compartmental model to emission tomography (PET) data

messages.author: 20edb03c469c5bd5
messages.subject: Modeling and fitting a compartmental model to emission tomography (PET) data
parts:
Dear Stan users,

it's the first time I write to this list and that is because I am still trying to understand if learning R and Stan could be worth the effort (I am new to both the main R language and, obviously, Stan) for what I am willing to try.

My idea is to try to fit a compartmental model for dynamic PET kinetic analysis (that is a system of 2 differential equation whose solution is then convoluted with the blood input function, check HERE for a reference ) using a bayesian approach. I should have from literature a set of prior distributions to try out (and then hopefully extend of change) but I am not sure if Stan is suitable for such a task or not.

If it could be, then the following question would be "how" to do it, but I think and like to proceed one step at a time ...

I really hope you can open my eyes on the R world.

Kind regards,

Michele

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Modeling and fitting a compartmental model to emission tomography (PET) data
parts:
Stan lets you fit models that involve parametric diff eqs.
The manual explains how and there's a case study for
soil carbon models here:

http://mc-stan.org/documentation/case-studies.html

It was the first case study, so it's way at the bottom.

There is also a lot of tutorial material one level up under
"DOCS".

- Bob
